overview.oneLineTake: The AI spending trade is cracking while macro runs hot, so expect NQ to lead lower and avoid selling cheap downside premium in megacap tech until earnings digest.
themes: AI capex backlash is now the dominant tape. Alphabet fell nearly 13% in its worst day ever after a search revenue miss, ServiceNow dropped 27%, and QQQ closed down 1.4% at 715.34 while SPY held at 769.36.

After hours piled on: Intel sank about 21% on weak PC guidance, and Amazon slid despite 39% AWS growth after posting negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion. Nasdaq 100 futures are lower into the Asia session.
Rotation, not liquidation. Small caps and breadth held up while megacap tech sold off, so the damage is concentrated in index heavyweights.
Macro is running hot. Q3 GDP printed 3.4% and September PCE inflation accelerated, a day after the Fed held with two dissents for a hike.
Oil is firming on signs the US may resume strikes on Iran, feeding the inflation story.
risks: Hike risk is back on the table with hot growth, firmer inflation, and a 10-year yield near 5%.
Index concentration: further megacap guidance cuts drag NQ harder than the broad market.
Credit stress: European junk spreads at their widest since 2009, plus rising Google debt risk gauges.
Crypto contagion after a possible Binance hack, with $2.54 billion in stablecoins frozen.
Iran escalation could spike crude and rates together.

intelligence.headline: Investors May Have Bought All the AI Bonds They Can Handle
intelligence.summary: Early signs suggest the credit market is nearing the limit of how much AI buildout debt it can absorb, with yields on some data center bonds and loans in double digits and CDS on Broadcom, SpaceX and Oracle debt spiking to junk-like levels.

intelligence.headline: Wall Street's AI Debt Machine Is Starting to Choke on Supply
intelligence.summary: Bankers are finding it harder to offload risk, and Morgan Stanley's Carolyn Campbell said top-rated data center bonds now yield closer to 7%, up from below 5% at the start of 2026.

intelligence.headline: Pimco Offloads Billions in AI Debt Just in Time to Skirt Losses
intelligence.summary: Pimco, which lent billions to the AI debt market in 2025, cut positions just in time to avoid losses.

intelligence.headline: Alphabet Tumbles After Disappointing Revenue
intelligence.summary: Alphabet fell 10% after sales underwhelmed, reinforcing concerns Google is losing ground to AI rivals despite heavy AI spending.

intelligence.headline: Samsung Shares Slide After Return Plan Is Delayed
intelligence.summary: Samsung disappointed and left investors waiting for details of a new shareholder return plan; Nasdaq futures sank 1%.

intelligence.headline: Marvell Said to Near Deal for Lumentum
intelligence.summary: Marvell is in talks to buy Nvidia-backed data center optics maker Lumentum, which has a market value of $83 billion.

intelligence.headline: Lagarde Will Step Down as ECB President
intelligence.summary: Christine Lagarde said she will leave the ECB in early 2027, starting the race to replace her.

intelligence.headline: ECB Set to Hold Rates
intelligence.summary: The ECB is expected to keep interest rates on hold today.

intelligence.headline: Fed Holds as Warsh Telegraphs More Hikes
intelligence.summary: The Fed held, while Kevin Warsh signaled the potential for more hikes without explicitly saying it.

intelligence.headline: Microsoft Gains on Azure Sales
intelligence.summary: Microsoft rose 3.5% as surging Azure cloud sales showed AI spending is paying off.

intelligence.headline: ServiceNow Falls as Outlook Revives AI Fears
intelligence.summary: ServiceNow sank 18% and Fortinet 25% on outlooks; Salesforce fell 4.3%, Palo Alto Networks 5.8% and CrowdStrike 5.5%.

intelligence.headline: Chipotle Sales Beat on New Menu
intelligence.summary: Chipotle rose 7.2% as new menu launches boosted sales; Eli Lilly and Caterpillar report before the bell, Amazon, Intel and Coinbase after the close.

intelligence.headline: Latin America Stock Fund Collapse Deepens
intelligence.summary: Only 226 Latin America-dedicated funds remain globally, down from over 660 in 2015, and Brazilian stocks collapsed this week after Lula's surprise re-election.

intelligence.headline: European Earnings Growth to Rival US
intelligence.summary: European company earnings are expected to grow 23% in Q3, just shy of the 24% forecast for the S&P 500.
